From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: stakeholder heatmap + exception proposal

Hi Sarah — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side.

Call recap
- Confirmed scope: pilot of Redwood inference for intake routing + summary generation (QA/volumetrics: ~6k requests/day, median seq length 300 tokens).
- Decision criteria: reliability (SLOs), cost/unit, and security attestations (SOC 2 + data residency).
- Key stakeholders you named: Emily Park (CFO, economic buyer), Sarah Powell (Dir. Data Platforms, technical buyer), Procurement team (procurement@medbridge.com), and Legal (J. Doe).

Attachments: I attached a stakeholder heatmap (medbridge-stakeholder-heatmap.xlsx) that maps influence/impact and a brief exception proposal draft (exception-proposal-draft.pdf).

Ask / proposed next steps
1) Can you confirm Emily Park is the final economic approver and whether we should engage her directly now or wait until procurement intake is submitted?
2) You mentioned procurement would need an SLA that matches enterprise standards. To keep the pilot moving, wed like to propose a scoped SLA exception: 99.95% uptime limited to the pilot (6 months) with a credit schedule tied to monthly availability.
3) Pricing: given the pilot profile, were proposing an introductory credit/discount for onboarding. Please confirm whether a one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) is acceptable vs. a recurring discount.
4) Please share the procurement intake form (if you have a templated doc) and any primary legal contacts besides J. Doe so we can send SOC2 evidence and a tidy data-retention statement.

If youre comfortable, Ill turn this into a formal exception request for your procurement/legal review and share the exact SLA wording and credit schedule.

Thanks — Ben

Thanks Ben — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirmed: Emily Park is the economic approver and will sign off on commercial terms, though procurement will gate the contracting timeline. Ill introduce you to Emily after procurement confirms intake (we try to limit direct exec outreach until paperwork is in).
- Procurement timeline: intake goes in this week; typical review 7-14 business days for pilot agreements. Im copying procurement@medbridge.com so they can attach the intake form.
- Legal asks: J. Doe (copied) will want SOC 2 Type II evidence, encryption at rest details, and a short data retention/erasure statement for pilot data.

Procurement attached: medbridge-procurement-intake.pdf — please fill and return. For the SLA exception: procurement/legal will expect a formal request document enumerating the exact SLA percentages, credit schedule, and the pilot scope/duration. Please provide that as a PDF.

On pricing: procurement prefers one-off credits for pilots rather than permanent list-price discounts. Providing a clear start/end date makes approval easier.

Ill coordinate internally and flag Emily once procurement intake is in.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Sarah Powell <sarah.powell@medbridge.com>

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: stakeholder heatmap + exception proposal — internal routing / approval request

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding the exchange with MedBridge. The ask from procurement/legal will be a formal SLA/discount exception for a 6-month pilot. Ive attached the draft exception proposal wed submit (exception-proposal-draft.pdf). Key points / rationale: 

Summary of recommendation
- Pilot scope: limited to routing + summarization for intake (6 months).
- SLA ask: 99.95% uptime for pilot window (we normally document 99.9% in hosted tiers). Provide credit schedule: 5% credit for monthly availability between 99.5-99.95, 10% below 99.5.
- Commercial ask: one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of the first-month invoice to offset integration work. No permanent list-price change.
- Security/legal deliverables: SOC2 Type II report, data-residency and retention statement, encryption in transit/rest. 

Why approve (business impact)
- Strategic: MedBridge is a priority healthcare prospect in mid-market with a fast pilot pipeline and potential for Dedicated later.
- Revenue upside: forecasted expansion to Dedicated capacity if pilot meets uptime and quality targets (expected ARR uplift if successful).

Risks / proposed guardrails
- Limit exception to pilot only (explicit end-date).
- Require signed pilot MSA addendum that scopes SLA and credits.
- Escalation: if availability drops below thresholds twice in the pilot, we will revert to standard pricing for subsequent months.

Request
- Approval to proceed with the proposed SLA exception and 20% onboarding credit (one-time), or counter-propose an alternate percentage. If approved, Ill finalize the exception doc and send to procurement/legal this afternoon.

Quoted from Sarahs email below for context.

— Ben

Ben — thanks for the clear summary and materials. I approve moving forward with an exception request with the following modifications and controls: 

Approvals / conditions
1) Discount: approve a pilot onboarding credit but cap it at 15% of first-month invoice (not 20%). The rationale: marketing/sales credits need a finance sign-off above 15% for sustained discounts. We can include a one-time credit schedule of 15% with a documented clause that any additional commercial concession requires Revenue Ops approval.
2) SLA: approve the 99.95% pilot SLA exception for a 6-month term only. Ensure the draft MSA addendum restricts the SLA to pilot scope and includes an automatic revert to standard SLA/pricing after pilot end.
3) Legal/Finance routing: route the completed exception package (final PDF, credit calculation, SLA addendum) to Legal (j.doe@medbridge.com) and Finance Ops for review. I will loop in Revenue Ops if the final credit exceeds the 15% cap.
4) Measurement: include a monitoring/tracing plan and a runbook for incident response and post-incident RCA; CS should confirm instrumentation with the customer.

Please prepare the final exception packet today and send it to procurement and legal. Attach the HubSpot deal link and include the Dealmaker ID in the packet. Ill approve sign-off to ship once Legal confirms SOC2 evidence is sufficient and Finance Ops acknowledges the credit schedule.

Related links / refs
